findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so an anonymous denial wrongly denies the renderer
findings.body:
`userPermDenialCacheKey` is built from `checkReq.UserUID` and does not include `checkReq.IdentityType`. Both anonymous and renderer subjects use UID `0` (`anonymous:0` and `render:0`, see service_test.go:803 and service_test.go:853), so both end up with the same key, `<ns>.perm_0_<action>_<name>_<folder>`.

Here is how it breaks. An anonymous Viewer is denied `dashboards:read` on dashboard X in folder F, which stores the denial at line 154. For the next 30s, a renderer Check for the same X/F hits the denial cache at line 117 and returns `Allowed: false`. That happens before `getRendererPermissions` (line 446) is reached, even though that function always grants `dashboards:read`. Image rendering then fails, and no error explains why. The reverse also happens: when the renderer is denied an action, anonymous is denied it too.

Fix: put the identity type in the denial key, e.g. `userPermDenialCacheKey(ns, string(idType)+":"+uid, …)`, or skip the denial cache for `TypeRenderService`.

findings.title: Ambiguous `_` separator lets different (name, folder) pairs share a denial entry
findings.body:
The key joins `name` and `parent` with `_`, but Grafana dashboard and folder UIDs can contain `_`. So `(name="a_b", folder="c")` and `(name="a", folder="b_c")` both produce `…_a_b_c`. A denial cached for the first pair silently denies the second for `shortCacheTTL` (30s), even when the user has access to it.

Fix: use a separator that cannot appear in UIDs, or length-prefix or escape the components. Medium confidence because I did not re-check the UID charset validation in this snapshot.

findings.title: "explicit cache deny" test passes even with the denial cache removed
Every first-time denial now goes to the permission DB query instead of the cached scope map
findings.body: Before this change, `getUserPermissions` served the scope map from `permCache` for 30s, whatever the Check outcome. Now a cached map that denies falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, and that function no longer reads `permCache` (the read was removed at line 379). The denial cache is keyed per name and folder, so a user who is denied N distinct dashboards triggers N `permissionStore.GetUserPermissions` queries. `singleflight` only merges concurrent calls. Workloads that filter many resources through Check (search results, for example) will see much more DB load. Consider rate-limiting the refresh per user and action, e.g. refresh only when the cached entry is older than a few seconds.

findings.title: User identifier lookup runs twice on cache miss or error
findings.body: `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `GetUserIdentifiers`. If that lookup fails (unknown user, DB error), Check and List fall back to `getIdentityPermissions` → `getUserPermissions`, which calls `GetUserIdentifiers` again (line 374). Failures are not cached, so every failing request makes two `store.GetUserIdentifiers` round-trips. Consider returning the identifiers, or the error, from the cached lookup so the fallback can reuse them.

contracts.action: Check consults the new per-resource denial cache before anything else
contracts.equivalent_path: permCache lookups in getCachedIdentityPermissions / getUserPermissions, keyed by resolved user UID
contracts.before_after: Before: no per-resource denial cache; the scope map was cached for 30s. After: a hit returns deny immediately, and any DB-derived deny is stored for shortCacheTTL. The key has no identity type, and anonymous and renderer share UID 0.
contracts.visible_effect: An anonymous denial causes the renderer to be denied the same resource for 30s, so rendering fails.
contracts.failure_mode: Cache Get errors are logged in cacheWrap.Get and treated as a miss; Set errors are logged and ignored.

contracts.action: Cached scope map used first in Check and List; a deny from the cache falls back to the DB
contracts.equivalent_path: getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions previously read permCache before the singleflight DB fetch
contracts.before_after: Before: a cache hit was authoritative for both allow and deny. After: allow from the cache is authoritative; deny triggers a fresh DB fetch, and getUserPermissions no longer reads the cache, so the DB fetch always runs.
contracts.visible_effect: New grants are visible immediately unless a denial for the same resource is still cached. DB load rises for denials.
contracts.failure_mode: An error in the cached lookup (e.g. GetUserIdentifiers) is swallowed and the DB path runs, which repeats the lookup and reports its error.

contracts.action: In-process authz client now uses NoopCache instead of a 30s local cache
contracts.before_after: Before: in-proc Check/List results were cached client-side for 30s. After: every call reaches rbac.Service, which applies its own caches.
contracts.visible_effect: Permission changes are visible sooner in-proc, and every check makes an in-proc gRPC call.
contracts.failure_mode: NoopCache.Get returns cache.ErrNotFound. I could not read the authlib client source to confirm that it treats ErrNotFound as a miss and not as an error.
contracts.open_question: Does authlib's authz client handle cache.ErrNotFound from Get as a miss, and does it use the cache for anything besides Check/List results?

summary:
The PR adds a per-resource denial cache to Check. It tries the cached scope map first in Check and List, and falls back to the DB when the cached map denies. The in-process client now uses a no-op cache. I found three problems to fix and two to consider.

Fix:
- **Denial key collision between anonymous and renderer (high confidence).** The denial key has no identity type, and both anonymous and renderer use UID `0`. A recent anonymous denial makes the renderer fail on the same dashboard for 30s.
- **`_` separator collision (medium confidence).** The denial key joins name and folder with `_`, which UIDs can contain, so different name/folder pairs can share one entry and deny each other. I did not re-check the UID charset rules in this snapshot.
- **Ineffective test.** The "explicit deny" test stores `false` where it means `true`, so it passes even without the denial cache.

Consider:
- Every first-time denial now runs the permission DB query, a perf regression.
- The user identifier lookup runs twice when it fails.

One question is still open: I could not read the authlib client source, so I have not confirmed it treats `cache.ErrNotFound` from `NoopCache` as a cache miss.
